regressions.note: A lone trailing DLE flushes the data before it and buffers the DLE; the next feed decides whether it was an escape or a frame. Chunked and single feeds emit different numbers of data events for this stream.
Raw DLE/STX bytes inside a control payload are covered by the length header and must not be rescanned as framing.
A frame split at every single code point, with a 3-byte code point in the payload: byte-length header vs code-point-indexed buffer walk.

Found by explore_control_channel_fuzz.py. Data that precedes a frame the decoder later rejects is DELIVERED when the feed is split (an earlier feed() already returned it) and DISCARDED when the whole stream arrives at once (the raise throws away the events built so far). Same bytes, same error, different delivery.

serializer_divergences.note: CPython keeps int/float apart through JSON; Go, .NET and JS all write 0.
Same, inside an array, next to a value that really is fractional.
Go and .NET escape U+2028/U+2029; CPython and JS emit them raw.
.NET escapes DEL (U+007F); the other three emit it raw.
.NET writes \uXXXX escapes with upper-case hex digits (\u001F); the other three use lower case.
.NET writes astral code points as a \uXXXX surrogate pair; CPython, Go and JS emit raw UTF-8.
